column75:
All the chronic conditions I have are inflammatory and one of them flaring up impacts on all the others, so I end up in a vicious cycle of inflammation, pain and fatigue. I wonder how common multiple inflammatory co-morbidities is for other endo sufferers?
I am interested in the link between hormones and endo. I had been on the pill for approx 10years with 1 break from it during that period. During that break, I developed asthma and GERD. The asthma presented with multiple chest infections and frequent antibiotics over a two year period as a result. 
The GnRH injections resulted in fibromyalgia and kickstarted perimenopause at 35. I wonder how often this reaction has been seen in endo sufferers?
 I’ve been dealing with debilitating symptoms since then and I trialled HRT to see if it would alleviate some of the symptoms. It began to improve my sleep, fatigue, IBS-C symptoms amongst other things but it flared up my pelvic and period pain and bowel movement pain to a high degree. 
I feel that the hormonal treatments for endo can be a bit of a blunt instrument - that shutting down your hormones to control symptoms has undocumented consequences and knock on effects. I think the level to which endo patients with hormone imbalances need nuanced, tailored hormone treatment is not considered or available at present.

column75:
Hormonal treatments - I had to try some before we found one that treated my endometriosis. When on the hormone treatments which weren't suitable for my disease, my mental health was adversely affected. I would cry uncontrollably at only mildly sad TV programmes and I would feel slightly depressed. I would feel like I was 2 different people, I would know that there was nothing wrong but couldn't control the emotions. 
Food: I would eat a "normal" plain meal and one day I would be fine and another day, I would faint with the pain of my bowel to rush to exclude what I had just eaten. 
Iron/  Vit B 12
Due to huge flooding at menstruation time I would always be anemic and despite trying every iron supplement my body wouldn't absorb iron. I would have chronic wind and be very uncomfortable and bloated from oral iron or from iron rich foods.  I also suffer from very low levels of Vit B 12 as a result of the massive blood loss every month. 

From ages 16 - 25 when I was actually diagnosed, I felt that what I was sufferings was in my head and that it wasn't actually real because of the lack of understanding of the disease. I am now 47 and I feel very strongly that all young girls in secondary school should be made aware of the condition and that it is "manageable" and not go through the mental anguish of feeling "im mad" like I did or I need to have a baby to stop feeling like this which was what was said to me at the time.

I tried as much as I could to not take any pill, especially because they didn't really help. Then they diagnosed me with adenomyosis in July and told me that I have to do another surgery (2nd in less than 5 years). They said that to preserve my fertility I need to go on the pill. 
This shouldn't happen. I shouldn't have to take hormones that shut down my personality to be able to function as a normal person and maybe be mother one day. 
Thank you for researching this disease. I hope you find a better way to target it.

column73:
I removed caffeine, most processed foods, alcohol, smoking, excessive red meat, saucy foods unless in small amounts paired with vegetables. 

I don’t eat cows dairy but goats and sheep’s is ok. 

I avoid gluten as much as possible. 

My regular therapies include yoga, acupuncture, lymphatic drainage massage, meditation. 

I exercise everyday with gentle walking and a I do gentle running. I also enjoy weights in moderation and swimming but I can’t push myself too hard or I get a flare up. 

I take the following supplements most days: NAC, omega, vitamin b12, berberine, inistol, magnesium. 

I try to remove endocrine disrupting chemicals such as scented things, I don’t wear make up a lot, I don’t use cleaning products unless natural or without using gloves. I don’t drink tap water. 

I always drink very strong non caffeinated herbal teas like loose peppermint and rooibus. 

I eat protein regularly to keep my insulin levels normal and try to eat a very high fibre diet. I try to not eat after 7pm and I try to drink a lot of water. 

I sleep for 8+ hours a night.

I’m super sensitive to smells, light.

This was over 20 years ago and so there was no connection to endometriosis ever mentioned by my gp. In my early 20s I went on the pill until I was 35, i never had any endo symptoms during this time. the leg pain only returned when I came off the pill. 
The leg pain appears to be a symptom of endo but not one that gets talked about enough and I image ignored in some cases. I didn't have to fight for a diagnosis as my fertility clinic suggested I had endo and I was referred to the beacon. Had a lap and stage 2 endo was found. After my surgery I had 3 months of no symptoms and then they came back worse than ever.  There is no otc pain relief that helps with the pain nor ponstan which I was prescribed again in recent years.
The only thing that helped ease the leg pain was a very hot hot water bottle placed on my legs as I lay down.
